subject: Liability cap proposal — anchoring vs annual smoothing
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Liability cap proposal — anchoring vs annual smoothing

Patricia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to put two concrete approaches on the table for the MSA / Order Form cap so your procurement and legal teams can react quickly. Attached is our current redline with inline notes (RWI_MSA_redline_20260509.docx).

Two options we can pursue:

Option A — Annualized, reset each year
- Cap = 1.5x the fees invoiced to ACME in the prior 12 months (resets each anniversary).
- Covers most liability other than excluded items below.

Option B — Contract-term aggregate anchor
- Cap = 2.0x total fees paid under the contract term (one-time aggregate cap).

Proposed carve-outs (not subject to cap):
- IP indemnity payments,
- Claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence,
- Breach of confidentiality of customer data,
- Third-party IP claims where indemnity applies.

Additional notes:
- We prefer an annualized approach when customers have variable monthly consumption — it ties exposure to recent usage.
- If you have a procurement rule that disallows multipliers >1x, we can discuss limiting multipliers to 1.0 but narrowing exclusions for a better balance.

Next steps: can you share ACME's preference (Option A vs B), any internal ceiling constraints (e.g., max multiple allowed), and your legal team's preferred wording for carve-outs? If helpful, we can add a fallback SLO-credit mechanism for certain availability incidents to reduce reliance on cash damages.

Attachments: RWI_MSA_redline_20260509.docx, OrderForm_Spend_Scenarios_20260509.xlsx

— Rachel

Subject: Re: Liability cap proposal — anchoring vs annual smoothing

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear options and the redline. Procurement pushed back during our internal read: ACME policy typically caps liability at 1.0x annual spend (we use annualized ceilings for cloud SaaS deals). An aggregate multiplier above 1x is usually a non-starter unless there are very narrow carve-outs.

A couple of asks from legal/procurement:
- Can you provide a version where the multiplier is 1.0x but with tightened exclusions (we would ask to limit exclusions to: IP indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct, and regulatory fines where law requires)?
- We would prefer annual reset (Option A) vs. aggregate if you must choose.

I attached our annotated comments (ACME_comments_20260509.pdf) — there are line edits on the MSA exclusions and a requested definition for "fees paid" (they want to confirm invoiced vs collected).

If you can get a narrow counterproposal by EOD Monday, procurement will escalate to our head of sourcing.

— Patricia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Liability cap proposal — anchoring vs annual smoothing

Team —

I reviewed ACME's annotated comments. Short framing from legal: we should aim for a commercially acceptable compromise that preserves our operational exposure management while meeting ACME procurement constraints. My recommended counter:

- Core: Annual reset cap at 1.0x annual fees (aligns to ACME policy).
- Tradeoff: Keep a small set of exclusions but tighten the language and add a specific carve-in for SLO-credit resolution.

Specifically:
1) Cap definition
   - "Cap" means the greater of: (a) total fees paid by Customer during the preceding 12 months, and (b) $100,000, per-12-month computation; resets each anniversary. (This preserves a floor for low-spend pilots.)
2) Multiplier
   - No multiplier (1.0x) to satisfy procurement.
3) Exclusions (exceptions to the Cap) — limited to:
   - IP indemnity obligations;
   - Damages resulting from wilful misconduct or gross negligence;
   - Legal obligations that cannot be limited by law (e.g., certain statutory fines).
   - Data confidentiality breach: allow for remediation costs and regulatory fines, but cap third-party compensatory damages — suggest explicit carve language that balances both sides.
4) SLO credits
   - Where a claim arises solely from availability/performance incidents covered under published SLOs, parties shall resolve by SLO-credit mechanism per the Order Form; only if bona fide material damage beyond the SLO credits is demonstrable does the monetary cap apply.

Rationale: aligns to customer procurement, retains protection for us via a reasonable floor, and channels operational incidents into SLO mechanics where appropriate.

I'll draft the updated redline wording for the MSA and the Order Form clause; Rachel / Marissa, if you want to soften the floor number or propose a different floor for enterprise deals, say so.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Liability cap proposal — anchoring vs annual smoothing

Patricia —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing ACME's comments. Our legal team dug in and we think there's a pragmatic path that should satisfy procurement while protecting both sides. High-level counterproposal (attached as a short clause we can drop into the MSA):

- Cap: Annual reset cap equal to Fees paid by Customer during the preceding 12 months, subject to a floor of $150,000 (i.e., the greater of 12-month fees and $150k).
- No multiplier applied (1.0x).
- Exclusions from the cap limited to: (i) Redwood's indemnity obligations for third-party IP infringement; (ii) damages resulting from willful misconduct or gross negligence; (iii) legal obligations that cannot be limited by applicable law.
- Data breach wording: for claims arising from a confidentiality/data breach, Redwood's liability shall include regulatory fines and reasonable third-party remediation costs; however, compensatory damages paid to a Customer shall still be subject to the Cap unless resulting from willful misconduct.
- SLO mechanism: for incidents covered by published SLOs, the parties will first apply the SLO-credit schedule in the Order Form; only material compensatory damages demonstrably exceeding SLO credits will flow to a monetary claim under the Cap.

We've kept a modest floor to protect RWI for low-spend pilots and to ensure we can remediate serious incidents. If ACME insists on removing the floor, we can consider substituting a short-duration warranty escrow or additional insurance requirement for pilot programs.

Please see the attached short redline snippet and a clean copy for your procurement team (RWI_MSA_redline_20260509.docx). If that looks workable, Karthik can incorporate the exact clause language for DocuSign and we can route to your head of sourcing.

Next steps: can you confirm late Tue (COB Tuesday) whether procurement can accept the floor + 1.0x structure? If yes, we will finalize redlines and prepare the order form PO template.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Liability cap proposal — anchoring vs annual smoothing

Rachel / Karthik —

Appreciate the compromise language and the floor explanation. Procurement and legal have reviewed: the annual reset + 1.0x approach with a floor is acceptable in principle, but they want the floor lowered to $100k for pilot accounts and a clause that the floor steps up to an enterprise-tier floor once annualized spend exceeds $2M (i.e., different floors by tier).

Legal liked the tightened exclusions and the SLO-first escalation. Please incorporate the tiered floor language and send a final redline for DocuSign. Also send the updated Order Form showing the SLO-credit table and the PO template so procurement can route a PO quickly.

If you can return the final redline by EOD tomorrow, we can proceed with signature and start provisioning.

— Patricia
Patricia Gomez
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Corporation
